title: Lifting reachability along an edge set
statement: Let $\mathit{edges}$ and $\mathit{edges}'$ be two lists of weighted edges on $n$ vertices, and suppose that whenever two vertices $a$ and $b$ are symmetrically adjacent in $\mathit{edges}$ — that is, some edge of $\mathit{edges}$ has endpoints $\{a,b\}$ — the vertices $a$ and $b$ are connected by a path through $\mathit{edges}'$. Then for any vertices $u$ and $v$, if $u$ and $v$ are connected by a path through $\mathit{edges}$, they are also connected by a path through $\mathit{edges}'$.
hypotheses_covered: every symmetric adjacency in edges yields reachability in edges'
u and v are reachable through edges
replaced:
If every symmetric adjacency in $\mathit{edges}$ implies reachability in
$\mathit{edges}'$, and $\mathtt{Reach}\,\mathit{edges}\,u\,v$, then
$\mathtt{Reach}\,\mathit{edges}'\,u\,v$.
